summary: Verified web (light mode) header separators fix in /app/frontend/src/components/Layout.jsx (lines 299 & 302). BUG FIX IS NOT EFFECTIVE: both separator spans still have computed background-color rgba(0,0,0,0) (transparent) in light mode at a desktop viewport (1440x900). Visually confirmed in a zoomed screenshot — no vertical line is drawn between the notifications/account-health group, the ParticipantSwitcher, and the AccountMenu. Root cause: the Tailwind opacity modifier /30 only applies to colours defined in the Tailwind theme; `primary-k` is a custom utility class declared in index.css (line 256: `.bg-primary-k { background-color: var(--kindred-primary); }`), so `bg-primary-k/15` and `bg-primary-k/30` are BOTH no-op classes — neither produced a background. Changing /15 to /30 made no difference. Dashboard regression: PASSES — Caregiver dashboard for samburke@test.com loads fully (greeting 'Good afternoon, Sam.', 'Viewing care for Sam Burke', walk-through card, 6 action cards including Upload a Statement / Check an Invoice / Ask Wayly a Question / Draft a Letter / Check a Price / All Tools). No layout breakage, no new console errors (only pre-existing GSI_LOGGER origin warnings unrelated to this change).

ui_bugs.issue: The two vertical dividers remain INVISIBLE in light mode. Computed background-color on both <span> elements is rgba(0,0,0,0). The /30 opacity modifier produces no CSS rule because `primary-k` is not a Tailwind theme colour — it is a hand-written utility in /app/frontend/src/index.css:256 (`.bg-primary-k { background-color: var(--kindred-primary); }`). Tailwind therefore does not emit a `.bg-primary-k\/30` rule, and the class is silently dropped. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/Layout.jsx:299 and :302.

issues: Visual separators between notifications/account-health, 'caring for' pill, and account menu are absent — the three controls run together without any divider in light mode, which is exactly the bug the fix was meant to address.

action_items: Replace the no-op `bg-primary-k/30` class on Layout.jsx:299 and :302 with something that actually paints a background. Three equivalent options, in order of preference:

(a) Arbitrary value with the CSS var: className='hidden lg:block h-6 w-px mx-1' plus style={{ backgroundColor: 'rgba(14,77,82,0.3)' }} — immediate, no CSS edit needed. (--kindred-primary is #0E4D52 = rgb(14,77,82).)

(b) Add a dedicated utility to /app/frontend/src/index.css next to `.bg-primary-k`: `.bg-primary-k\/30 { background-color: rgba(14,77,82,0.3); }` (and similarly /15 if it is used elsewhere). Then the existing className keeps working.
(c) Register `primary-k` as a proper theme colour in tailwind.config.js so Tailwind's slash-opacity syntax generates the rule automatically — longer blast radius but cleanest.

After applying, re-verify with a 1440x900 viewport in light mode: the two dividers should render as faint teal vertical 1px x 24px lines at header-right, and computed background-color should NOT be rgba(0,0,0,0).

rca of the issue: Direct cause: both separator spans compute background-color = rgba(0,0,0,0) (transparent) in light mode. Evidence: JS runtime check returned `[{bg: 'rgba(0,0,0,0)', w:1, h:24, ...}, {bg: 'rgba(0,0,0,0)', w:1, h:24, ...}]` after login. Mechanism: Tailwind's slash-opacity syntax (`bg-primary-k/30`) only generates a CSS rule when the colour is declared in the Tailwind theme (tailwind.config.js). In this app `primary-k` is defined as a plain utility class in /app/frontend/src/index.css:256 (`.bg-primary-k { background-color: var(--kindred-primary); }`), so Tailwind never emits `.bg-primary-k\/30` — the token in the className is just ignored. The dividers fall back to the span's implicit transparent background and are therefore invisible on any light surface. Changing /15 to /30 moved from one invisible value to another invisible value. Mitigation: paint the background through a channel Tailwind actually processes — either an arbitrary-value class backed by the CSS var/rgb, a hand-written `.bg-primary-k\/30` rule in index.css, or promote `primary-k` to a tailwind.config.js theme colour.
